title: Attention and vision transformers
goal: Compute scaled dot-product attention by hand and explain how a vision transformer turns an image into tokens.
exercises: A ViT uses 16 × 16 patches on a 384 × 384 × 3 image. How many patch tokens are there, how long is each flattened patch, and how many entries does one head's attention matrix have once the class token is included?
Compute one attention row with d = 4: query q = (1, 0, 2, 1), keys k₁ = (2, 0, 0, 0) and k₂ = (0, 1, 1, 1), and scalar values v₁ = 4, v₂ = −2. Give the weights and the output.

The entries of q and k are independent with mean 0 and variance 1, and d = 256. What are the standard deviations of qᵀk and of qᵀk/√d? Compare the softmax of two scores two standard deviations apart before and after scaling.

Explain why the class-token output of a self-attention layer without positional embeddings does not change when you shuffle the patches, and name two assumptions a CNN builds in that a ViT has to learn.
solutions: 384/16 = 24 patches per side, so 24² = 576 patch tokens. Each flattened patch has 16 × 16 × 3 = 768 numbers. With the class token there are 577 tokens, so one head's attention matrix has 577² = 332,929 entries, about 8.6 times the 197² = 38,809 of a 224 × 224 image.

Var(qᵀk) = d × 1 × 1 = 256, so its standard deviation is 16; after dividing by √256 = 16 it is 1. Two scores two standard deviations apart differ by 32 before scaling: softmax gives (1 − 1.3×10⁻¹⁴, 1.3×10⁻¹⁴), a one-hot row with vanishing gradients. After scaling they differ by 2: softmax gives (0.881, 0.119), and both keys still receive gradient.

Without positional embeddings every score depends only on the contents of the two tokens. Shuffling the patches permutes the class token's scores and the value vectors in the same way, so the weighted sum Σⱼ aⱼvⱼ is unchanged; the patch outputs are permuted identically (permutation equivariance). A CNN assumes locality (small kernels see neighbouring pixels) and translation equivariance with shared weights; a ViT must learn spatial relations from its positional embeddings and from data.
checkpoint: Compute softmax(QKᵀ/√d)V for a small example, explain why the scores are divided by √d, and count the tokens and the attention cost for a given image and patch size.
